paper.title: Linear Contextual Bandits with Adversarial Corruptions

settings.name_in_paper: Corrupted linear contextual bandits (known corruption level C)
unmapped: Noise is bounded |eps_t(a)| <= R with zero conditional mean and conditional variance <= sigma_t^2(a); heteroscedastic
Learner observes the per-round variance bound sigma_t(a_t) along with the reward
Learner knows the noise range R
Corruption level normalized by (R+1): C = (1/(R+1)) sum_t sup_a |r_t'(a) - r_t(a)|
Adversary decides corrupted reward function before seeing the agent's (randomized) action
settings.definition_quote: We assume that for all $t \ge 1$ and all $\ab \in \cD_t$, $\|\ab\|_2 \le A$, $|\langle \ab, \bmu^* \rangle| \le 1$ and $\|\bmu^*\|_2 \le B$ almost surely. ... $|\epsilon_t(\ab)| \le R, \EE[\epsilon_t(\ab)|\cF_t] = 0, \EE[\epsilon_t^2(\ab)|\cF_t] \le \sigma_t^2(\ab)$. ... $C = \frac{1}{R + 1} \sum_{t = 1}^T \sup_{\ab \in \cD_t} |r_t'(\ab) - r_t(\ab)|$.

settings.name_in_paper: Corrupted linear contextual bandits (unknown corruption level C)
unmapped: Noise is bounded |eps_t(a)| <= R with zero conditional mean and conditional variance <= sigma_t^2(a); heteroscedastic
Learner observes the per-round variance bound sigma_t(a_t) along with the reward
Learner knows the noise range R
Adversary decides corrupted reward function before seeing the agent's (randomized) action
settings.definition_quote: The protocol between the agent and the adversary at each round $t \in [T]$ ... The adversary observes $\cD_t$, $r_t'(\ab)$, $\sigma_t(\ab)$ for all $\ab \in \cD_t$ and decides a corrupted reward function $r_t$ defined over $\cD_t$.

symbols.Lambda_T: sum_t sigma_t^2, sum of per-round variance bounds

conditions: <a, mu*> in [-1,1] for all a in D_t

source.label: thm:alg:1
source.quote: Set $\lambda = 1 / B^2$. Suppose $C = \Omega(1), R = \Omega(1)$, for all $t \ge 1$ and all $\ab \in \cD_t$, $\langle \ab, \bmu^* \rangle \in [-1, 1]$. Then with probability at least $1 - \delta$, the regret of Algorithm \ref{alg:2} is bounded as follows: $\regret(T) = \tilde{O}\left(C d \sqrt{\sum_{t = 1}^T \sigma_t^2} + CR \sqrt{dT}\right)$.

results.notes: Regret defined via means (pseudo-regret), stated to hold w.p. 1-delta over noise. Algorithm's confidence radius depends on t only, so treated as anytime. Remark 3: with sigma_t <= R degenerates to O~(CdR sqrt(T)).

symbols.Lambda_T: sum_t sigma_t^2, sum of per-round variance bounds

conditions: <a, mu*> in [-1,1] for all a in D_t

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Set $\lambda = 1/B^2$. Suppose that $C = \Omega(1)$, $R = \Omega(1)$, for all $t \ge 1$ and all $\ab \in \cD_t$, $\langle \ab, \bmu^* \rangle \in [-1, 1]$. Then with probability at least $1 - 3 \delta$, the regret of Algorithm \ref{alg:1} is bounded as follows: $$\regret(T) = \tilde{O}\left(C^2d\sqrt{\sum_{t = 1}^T \sigma_t^2} + C^2 R\sqrt{dT}\right). $$

results.notes: C unknown to the algorithm. Probability 1-3delta. Remark 10: with sigma_t <= R gives O~(C^2 d R sqrt(T)). Algorithm uses T for ell_max.

symbols.Delta_ctx: smallest per-round gap min_t Delta_t, Delta_t = gap between best and second-best action values in D_t

conditions: <a, mu*> in [-1,1] for all a in D_t

source.label: thm:gap dependent regret
source.quote: Suppose that $C = \Omega(1)$, $R = \Omega(1)$, for all $t \ge 1$ and all $\ab \in \cD_t$, $\langle \ab, \bmu^* \rangle \in [-1, 1]$. Then with probability at least $1 - 3 \delta$, the regret of Algorithm \ref{alg:1} is bounded as follows: $$\regret(T) =  \tilde{O}\left(\frac{1}{\Delta}\cdot C^2R^2d + \frac{1}{\Delta}\cdot d^2C^2 \max_{t \in[T]} \sigma_t^2\right). $$

results.notes: Gap is the minimum over rounds of Dani-et-al-style per-round gaps; declared as Delta_ctx. Remark 12: implies O~(R^2 d^2 C^2/Delta).
